correctness.rationale: The stationary backward stochastic convolution has a.s. finite positive random Gaussian variance V because the homogeneous multiplier has negative logarithmic growth: lambda/2+(lambda/s)E log(1-sU)<=-lambda/2. Splitting at first exponential event gives V=C+AVprime with C=(2D/lambda)(e^(lambda T)-1), A=e^(lambda T)(1-sU)^2. For p>0, V^(p/2) has finite expectation exactly when E A^(p/2)<1 and E C^(p/2)<infinity, equivalent to psi(p;s)<0; strict comparison handles the cutoff itself. Strict convexity ensures unique positive root beyond zero and 2<kappa<2/s. The third-divided-difference identity E_A f-E_B f=-(3/2)f[0,1/2,2,3]>0 for f(u)=(1-su)^p,p>2 orders the two roots for every s. At s=1/4 independent exact rational checks reproduce EU=1, EU^2=2 for both laws, multiplier fourth moments 17/32 and 481/1024, psi_A(4)=lambda/8 and psi_B(4)=-31lambda/256. Thus the first fourth moment diverges, the second equals 12288 D^2/(31lambda^2), and both variances equal 4D/lambda. Uniform compact convergence psi(z/s) to z/2+Ee^(-zU)-1 proves the two distinct asymptotic inverse-s cutoffs. A finite checker confirms algebra, not the perpetuity theorem for all real exponents.
